claims.text: High-load nanoindentation with 10-second hold periods will reveal discrete localized yielding events in FeNiCrMn HEA.
The discrete localized yielding events indicate the onset of microplasticity.
The proposed stepped-load method will reveal microplasticity earlier than conventional continuous load ramps.
The FeNiCrMn specimen is to be tested in a homogenized and annealed state.
The specimen has a microstructure typical of laboratory-prepared FeNiCrMn specimens.
Nanoindentation will use a controlled load ramp from approximately 10 mN to 300 mN with 10-second holds at each load increment.
Nanoindentation will be coupled with in situ SEM observation.
Testing will be performed at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
Grain boundaries and dislocation sources serve as nucleation sites for localized plastic deformation in the alloy.
Increasing and holding the indentation load produces stress concentrations that activate local dislocation movement.
Activated local dislocation movement produces early localized yielding events.
Localized yielding will be observed as discrete load drops or sudden displacement bursts during hold periods.
The load–displacement events will correlate with microplastic initiation visible in in situ SEM images.
Conventional continuously ramped nanoindentation does not exhibit similarly distinct microplasticity events at low loads.
The observed behavior is limited to localized microscale phenomena, and its quantitative relationship to bulk mechanical properties is uncertain.
